1 خَظَا لَحْمُهُ , (S, K,) aor. يَخْظُو, (S,) inf. n. خُظُوٌّ, (K,) His flesh was, or became, compact; (S, K;) as also خَظِى, (K in art. خظى,) mentioned, as well as the former, by IF, and also by Kz, who does not mention the former, (TA,) aor. يَخْظَى, inf. n. خَظًى; (K;) or خَظِىَ should not be said; (S;) or خَظَا is more common. (IF.) See also خَظَا and خَظَتَا voce خَاظٍ, below. ＝
-A2- خَظَاهُ ٱللّٰهُ God made him, or it, (namely, flesh,) big, or large; (K accord. to the TA;) or big and thick; (CK;) as also ↓ اخظاهُ . (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
